issues: The rewrite's headline 'Confidence slump piles pressure on chancellor ahead of budget' and its trail nowhere state that confidence fell 'at the fastest rate since Covid', a specific comparative claim the original makes that is dropped entirely rather than moved into the trail.

The rewrite drops the original's 'cost of living bites' and replaces it with the vaguer 'economic fallout... adding to the pressure on consumers', weakening a specific claim into something less precise.

The headline-and-trail pair drops the original's bad figure 'falls at fastest rate since Covid' rather than stating it plainly, and the copy (headline and trail only) offers no upside to justify softening it, breaking rule 5 on minimising a bad figure.

The rewrite's headline 'South Wales residents told to keep windows shut as a precaution' adds 'as a precaution', a characterisation of the instruction that is not in the original, which frames it only as a response to kerosene contamination, unsafe water and burning eyes.

The headline reframes the directive to keep windows shut as a reassuring 'precaution', softening the severity the original conveys (unsafe water, burning eyes, kerosene slicks), with no upside in the copy to justify the softer framing (rule 5); this adds uplift the copy does not contain for a story with no response reported.

The progress line 'More women in the sport are speaking out, breaking the culture of silence around the allegations' simply restates the headline's 'Surfers break their silence' and the trail's 'more women are now coming forward', adding nothing about what is being done, contrary to the requirement that it stand on its own.

The progress line 'Macron has already banned '"'"'illegitimate'"'"' protests and promises further steps on the demonstrations' merely repeats facts already given in the headline and trail, naming no distinct action and adding nothing new about what is being done.

The progress line 'The environment secretary is pushing back against the private rescue plan over concerns it would burden customers' repeats the trail's 'raised concerns that customers would face an undue burden from the £10bn rescue plan' almost exactly, adding no new information about what is being done.

The progress line 'The new routes follow the closure of the previous Afghan resettlement scheme last year' repeats the trail's 'follows the closure of the Afghan scheme last year' almost verbatim, adding nothing new about what is being done.

The rewrite's headline and trail drop the original's accusation that Farage is 'evading scrutiny', replacing it with the neutral 'demands a '"'"'clear and truthful account'"'"'', which loses the original's claim that he has been dodging rather than merely being asked for information.

The progress line 'Doctors say the pontiff's tumour has not spread, though doubts remain about his planned trip to South America next month' is a near-verbatim duplicate of the trail, failing to stand on its own as required.
